messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE employee (
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    City TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE shop (
    Shop_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Location TEXT,
    District TEXT,
    Number_products INT,
    Manager_name TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE hiring (
    Shop_ID INT,
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Start_from TEXT,
    Is_full_time bool,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Shop_ID) REFERENCES shop(Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE evaluation (
    Employee_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Year_awarded TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Bonus REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID)
);

What do you mean by “hard-working”? Your schema doesn’t have a direct “hard_working” flag, so we need a rule to identify them. Common options:

1) **Employees who received a bonus** (from `evaluation`)  
2) Employees with **bonus above a threshold** (e.g., > 1000)  
3) Employees with **bonuses in multiple years** (consistent performance)

Here are SQL templates for each—tell me which one you want.

### 1) Employees who received any bonus (and their bonus info)
```sql
SELECT e.Employee_ID, e.Name, e.Age, e.City,
       ev.Year_awarded, ev.Bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
ORDER BY ev.Bonus DESC, ev.Year_awarded DESC;
```

### 2) “Hard-working” = bonus above a threshold
```sql
SELECT e.Employee_ID, e.Name, e.Age, e.City,
       ev.Year_awarded, ev.Bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus > 1000;   -- change threshold
```

### 3) “Hard-working” = received bonuses in at least N years
```sql
SELECT e.Employee_ID, e.Name, e.Age, e.City,
       COUNT(*) AS years_with_bonus,
       SUM(ev.Bonus) AS total_bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
GROUP BY e.Employee_ID, e.Name, e.Age, e.City
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;    -- change N
```

Which definition do you want (1/2/3), and do you want to include their **shop info** (from `hiring`/`shop`) too?
I think option 2 sounds good. Include their shop info too.

```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name AS Employee_Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  h.Start_from,
  h.Is_full_time,
  s.Shop_ID,
  s.Name AS Shop_Name,
  s.Location,
  s.District,
  s.Manager_name,
  ev.Year_awarded,
  ev.Bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
JOIN hiring h
  ON h.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
JOIN shop s
  ON s.Shop_ID = h.Shop_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus > 1000   -- set your threshold here
ORDER BY ev.Bonus DESC, ev.Year_awarded DESC;
```
Make sure to look for the employee with the highest bonus amount in that category.

```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name AS Employee_Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  h.Start_from,
  h.Is_full_time,
  s.Shop_ID,
  s.Name AS Shop_Name,
  s.Location,
  s.District,
  s.Manager_name,
  ev.Year_awarded,
  ev.Bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
JOIN hiring h
  ON h.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
JOIN shop s
  ON s.Shop_ID = h.Shop_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus > 1000   -- threshold
  AND ev.Bonus = (
    SELECT MAX(Bonus)
    FROM evaluation
    WHERE Bonus > 1000
  );
```
Also, I want to return the name of the employee who meets the criteria.

```sql
SELECT
  e.Name AS Employee_Name
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus > 1000
  AND ev.Bonus = (
    SELECT MAX(Bonus)
    FROM evaluation
    WHERE Bonus > 1000
  );
```
Also, remember to consider the one-time bonus category for the employee that fits the criteria.

If by “one-time bonus category” you mean employees who received a bonus **in exactly one year**, and among those (with `Bonus > 1000`) you want the **highest bonus**, use:

```sql
WITH one_time AS (
  SELECT Employee_ID
  FROM evaluation
  GROUP BY Employee_ID
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
),
candidates AS (
  SELECT ev.Employee_ID, ev.Year_awarded, ev.Bonus
  FROM evaluation ev
  JOIN one_time ot ON ot.Employee_ID = ev.Employee_ID
  WHERE ev.Bonus > 1000
)
SELECT
  e.Name AS Employee_Name,
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  h.Start_from,
  h.Is_full_time,
  s.Shop_ID,
  s.Name AS Shop_Name,
  s.Location,
  s.District,
  s.Manager_name,
  c.Year_awarded,
  c.Bonus
FROM candidates c
JOIN employee e ON e.Employee_ID = c.Employee_ID
JOIN hiring h   ON h.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
JOIN shop s     ON s.Shop_ID = h.Shop_ID
WHERE c.Bonus = (SELECT MAX(Bonus) FROM candidates);
```

If “one-time bonus category” instead means something else (e.g., a special bonus type column), tell me how it’s represented in your data.
